endorsements.quote: Importantly, the model should provide not just point estimates but also measures of uncertainty, reflecting the confidence level of its predictions [ 21 ].
This interface should integrate seamlessly with existing electronic health record systems and clinical workflows.
To address this gap, AI-driven glaucoma management should be paired with community-based care models, telemedicine, and public health initiatives to improve follow-up care accessibility.

While deep learning models are powerful, they must be complemented by more transparent approaches, especially for aspects of the prediction task where the underlying relationships are relatively simple.
The interface should also provide some level of explainability, offering insights into which factors are most influencing the AI's predictions.
Beyond instrument standardization, ensuring that AI models perform reliably across diverse populations requires rigorous validation using local datasets.
Hybrid models of care—Healthcare systems should gradually phase in AI prescreening, allowing clinics to adjust resources while monitoring its impact on clinician workload and patient outcomes.

unlisted_practices: Pair AI-based prescreening with strategies such as task-shifting, telemedicine, and workflow optimization to prevent surges in patient demand from overwhelming specialists.
Validate AI performance using diverse imaging sources, including lower-cost and portable diagnostic tools.
Design AI models to degrade gracefully and adjust confidence levels when input data are incomplete or of lower quality.
Engage diverse community stakeholders, including patient advocates and community leaders, in AI deployment.
Design AI systems as assistive tools rather than replacements for clinician judgment to mitigate automation bias.

screen.reason: The paper describes a conceptual framework and implementation considerations/recommendations for an AI-driven glaucoma progression prediction system across healthcare settings, rather than presenting empirical data.
